clue.text: Strong metal protects our side as a safety device

indicators.note: a protector wraps around what it guards, so the metal's symbol goes round the other piece

parts.note: iron, a strong metal, has the chemical symbol Fe
our side is us, as opposed to them

explanation.surface: A sturdy piece of metal shielding our team serves as a safeguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire link that melts to break an overloaded circuit is a standard electrical safety device.

clue.text: Pine marten, say, at first in the distance

indicators.note: at first puts the animal's coat ahead of the yearning word

parts.note: the pine marten is valued for its fur, so the animal stands for its pelt
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: A pine marten spotted far off in the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine marten' reads as one animal, but Pine and marten split into separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong is a measure of length, an eighth of a mile, used in horse racing.

clue.text: Break Easter egg and put to one side

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters apart to be reassembled

explanation.surface: Crack a chocolate egg and set it aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to separate or set apart from others.

clue.text: Run off, agog to disrupt political faction

indicators.note: disrupting the letters throws them out of order, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An excitable crowd flees in order to break up a party grouping.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to the radical clique around Mao's widow, a notorious political faction in China.

clue.text: Upper classes addressed as knights, do we hear? Ridiculous!

parts.note: A and B are the top social grades in British market research

indicators.note: a question about hearing signals that the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: knights are called Sir, so being addressed so is being sirred

explanation.surface: An indignant question about grand people being called Sir.
explanation.walkthrough: A and B are the top grades of the British social classification used in marketing.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd means ludicrous or laughably unreasonable.

clue.text: Steal a march to fill vacancy at school?

definitions.meaning: to gain an advantage over rivals, to move in front
a school without a head teacher would need to obtain one

explanation.surface: Getting ahead of rivals by filling an empty post at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting in front of others is gaining advantage; whimsically, a school seeking a principal must obtain one.

clue.text: Peers interfere outrageously in capitalist system

indicators.note: acting outrageously means wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Lords meddling scandalously in the market economy.
explanation.definitionFit: An economy of private business with little state control is the capitalist model.

clue.text: Approving republican slogan?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., with O read as zero: no monarch

explanation.definitionFit: To OK is to approve; read as nought plus monarch, it voices an anti-monarchist cry for no crown.

clue.text: Prize deer swallowing earth

indicators.note: swallowing takes the other piece inside

parts.note: the roe is a small deer
a sett is a badger's earth or burrow

explanation.surface: A deer gulping down soil wins an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize at shows.

clue.text: Serious distance to travel for work so late

parts.note: grave means serious
a yard is a measure of distance
to shift is to move or travel

explanation.surface: Commuting a long way for a job that finishes very late.
explanation.definitionFit: The overnight work period, typically midnight to morning, is known by this name.

clue.text: Once again defends non-U compliments

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, as in redo

indicators.note: non- means without, so the letter U is taken away

parts.note: to defend is to guard; he guards
the letter U itself

explanation.surface: Someone repeatedly protects compliments that are not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is the old British label for speech not used by the upper class; here it just drops a U.
explanation.definitionFit: Regards are good wishes or compliments, as in 'give her my regards'.

clue.text: Worst place to service a car?

definitions.meaning: an informal idiom for the absolute worst
in motor racing, the area beside the track where cars are refuelled and repaired

explanation.surface: A grumble about the dreadful garage where you have a car serviced.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls the lowest possible state this, and racing teams service cars in trackside bays of that name.

clue.text: Too much to drink, but finished article between lunch and dinner times?

indicators.note: between places these words in the gap separating two others

parts.note: lunch is traditionally at one o'clock
dinner is often served at eight o'clock
finished means over, as in the game is over
the definite article is the

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy who has had too much in the hours between midday meal and evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The meal times are given as clock hours: lunch at one, dinner at eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for having drunk slightly too much alcohol, being mildly drunk.

clue.text: Good woman's name

parts.note: a woman is a lady, so woman's is lady's

explanation.surface: A virtuous woman's reputation, her good name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, so an example of a name.

clue.text: Problem inside gum? Suck this

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: paste is a gum or glue
an ill is a problem or trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble with your gums? Here is a lozenge to suck.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small sweet or medicated lozenge that one sucks.

clue.text: See feature short-change young hero

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look
the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: short means a letter is cut from the end

parts.note: to vary is to change

explanation.surface: Watch a bit of short-changing of a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Young Lochinvar is the dashing hero of a ballad in Walter Scott's poem Marmion.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's ballad opens 'O young Lochinvar is come out of the west', so he is the young hero.

clue.text: Clear out boxes, say, giving Daniel almost all the others

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe
the rest means all the others

explanation.surface: Someone clearing out cartons and giving Daniel nearly everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing away trees such as box shrubs from land is stripping it of woodland.

clue.text: Mean to study, returning to university with such income?

parts.note: near is an old word for mean or stingy

indicators.note: returning means the word for a study is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A miserly student heading back to university, living off income they did not work for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to university' signals U goes at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Income from investments rather than employment is called unearned, so this describes that kind of income.

clue.text: Wild animal turns up, tune that's played being something soothing

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the gnu is a wild antelope

indicators.note: a tune that's played is performed freely, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild beast appears as a soothing melody plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses GNU to UNG; 'that's played' rearranges TUNE to UENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An unguent is a soothing ointment or salve.

clue.text: Black bird crosses a cold city

indicators.note: the bird spans across the other letters, holding them within

parts.note: the crow is a black bird
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A dark bird flies over a chilly town.
explanation.definitionFit: An older English spelling of Krakow, the Polish city.

clue.text: With "I do" get married? Not any more

parts.note: to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: Saying the vows to get married, then no longer being married.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue before it: married? Not any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bereaved of a spouse is no longer married, the state that ended.

clue.text: Start to speak to chaplains, having run out in dark suit

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter
out means the letter goes missing

parts.note: padres are military chaplains
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Begin by talking to the chaplains, having fled in a dark suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a suit of cards, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades are one of the two black suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Greedy type going round store must take care, having poor concentration

indicators.note: going round puts the greedy type around the store

parts.note: a grasper is a grasping, greedy person
a shop is a store
to mind is to take care, as in mind the step

explanation.surface: A grasping shopper going around a store should be careful, being easily distracted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a mind that jumps from topic to topic, unable to concentrate.

clue.text: I mourn member of RAF, one in a thousand

indicators.note: in puts the airman between the other letters

parts.note: K is short for a thousand, as in 10K
LAC is a Leading Aircraftman in the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Grieving for an airman who was one in a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' just says the airman is a single member.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation of sorrow, equivalent to alas.

clue.text: But in turn I have to make out-of-the-way sort of action

indicators.note: turning a word round means reading it backwards

parts.note: save means but or except, as in all save one
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about getting out of someone's way.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive action is what a pilot or driver takes to get out of the way of danger.

clue.text: To deny knowledge of Ovid was mistaken

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong, so the letters are put in a wrong order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Claiming the Roman poet Ovid was wrong about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown or repudiate, refusing to acknowledge any connection or knowledge.

clue.text: Start to enjoy job seeing slag off

parts.note: to take to something is to begin to like it
a task is a job

explanation.surface: Starting to like a job that involves criticising people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slag off' is British slang for criticising harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke or reprimand someone severely, a milder version of criticising them harshly.

clue.text: Poke right inside school

indicators.note: inside puts the one letter within the group word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A jab at the right inside a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of whales, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke or jab with a finger or stick.
